## Episode Thesis

Erik Nordenskiöld of the independent asset manager Citroner said earnings expectations going into Q3 reporting season are very high. He warned that sell-side ratings on S&P 500 stocks are at record optimism, and he read that as a contrarian warning sign. With US 10-year yields above 5%, expected returns on fixed income and equities are converging, so he recommended diversifying into more risk premia, especially emerging-market government bonds and high yield. He frames the mood as short-term euphoria with long-term worry, including the risk of an AI bubble if earnings growth disappoints.
